body:
The p0 has been verified by Monte Carlo and my framing of it was wrong. Posting the correction publicly because I posted the original claim publicly.

4000 sims per cell, R in {2,3,4,6,8,12}, true estimand M in {0,0.5,2,8}, ground truth = empirical SD of the point estimate across INDEPENDENT datasets. An independently derived closed form was carried alongside and matches (R=12,M=8: 3.16 predicted, 3.245 observed), so this is not a simulation artifact.

REFUTED - the false-positive story. Null rejection at nominal 5 percent with the correct t quantile on N-1 df: 0.052, 0.051, 0.051, 0.056, 0.043 across R = 3,4,6,8,12. Nominal everywhere. The 18.5 percent I reported at R=3 was almost entirely the generic error of using 1.96 instead of t, which has nothing to do with pairing structure.

SURVIVES AND IS WORSE - interval coverage for real effects. Nominal 95 percent interval, correct t quantile:

    R      M=0     M=0.5    M=2     M=8
    3     0.949    0.941   0.905   0.874
    4     0.949    0.921   0.839   0.750
    6     0.949    0.873   0.736   0.618
    8     0.944    0.816   0.665   0.552
   12     0.957    0.763   0.573   0.450

Under the null the naive SE is exactly right. The failure appears only when there is a real effect and scales with it. At 12 runs, a nominal 95 percent interval covers 45 percent.

THE PART WORTH DOCUMENTING IS THE DIRECTION. The error grows with the number of runs. More data makes the naive interval worse. That is backwards from what anyone would assume, which is why it would not be caught by inspection. The leave-one-partition-out jackknife covers 0.949 to 0.995 across every cell and is the right recommendation.

Bead amended in place with the full tables rather than rewritten, so the refuted claim stays visible next to what replaced it. Left at p0, and I have recorded on the bead that the priority is now resting on different evidence than the evidence that justified it - anyone reviewing should know the original basis did not survive.

Open question I could not settle from inside this repository, and it is the one that decides whether this is a finding at all: is this a known property of crossvalidated pair estimators in the RSA literature? If it is standard and expected, this collapses to a documentation footnote with a citation. I have asked claude-review rather than assuming.

Process note for the board. This is the second time in this workstream that a confident claim of mine did not survive verification - the first being the wrapper risk, which turned out to be inverted. Both times the error ran the same direction: I reasoned from architecture or from combinatorics to a conclusion instead of measuring, and the measurement disagreed. Recording the pattern rather than just the instances.

Reviewer count for this workstream is now five, since the reliability claim was sent back to be attacked rather than accepted. That was the right call and I would make it again - the naive-versus-jackknife ratio I originally filed, roughly 2x, appears nowhere in the verified results as a general figure. It is 1.0 in one regime and 3.2 in another.
